title: Filtered six operations and the filtered Hom comparison
statement:
Use the finite-field, scheme and finite constant coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and the filtered categories, forgetful functor $\omega$, graded pieces and filtration truncations of [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category]. The truncations, $\omega$ and $\operatorname{gr}^p$ descend to exact functors of triangulated categories. They give functorial distinguished triangles
$$t^{\ge p}M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow t^{<p}M\longrightarrow t^{\ge p}M[1].$$
In these finitely filtered categories the graded pieces jointly detect zero objects. The same assertions hold in $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$.
For a separated finite-type morphism $f$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, the six operations on the finite-coefficient bounded constructible finite-Tor domains of [prop-functor-package] admit triangulated filtered lifts; use $Rf^!$ only with the exceptional admissibility required there. Forgetting filtration recovers the ordinary operations, and each covariant one-variable operation commutes with $\operatorname{gr}^p$. Tensor and internal Hom admit bifiltered lifts with
$$\operatorname{gr}^r(M\otimes^LN)\simeq\bigoplus_{p+q=r}\operatorname{gr}^pM\otimes^L\operatorname{gr}^qN,\qquad
\operatorname{gr}^rR\mathcal Hom^F(M,N)\simeq\bigoplus_{q-p=r}R\mathcal Hom(\operatorname{gr}^pM,\operatorname{gr}^qN).$$
The ordinary and exceptional adjunctions, composition, base-change and evaluation transformations used in the Verdier trace construction have compatible filtered lifts; under these identifications their graded maps are the ordinary transformations.
For $M,N\in D^bF(X,A)$, filtered global derived Hom is a bifiltered lift $H=R\operatorname{Hom}^F_X(M,N)\in DF(\mathbf{Ab})$ of ordinary global derived Hom, with
$$\operatorname{gr}^rH\simeq\bigoplus_{q-p=r}R\operatorname{Hom}_X(\operatorname{gr}^pM,\operatorname{gr}^qN),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{D^bF(X,A)}(M,N)\simeq H^0(\omega t^{\ge0}H).$$
The forgetful map to ordinary Hom is induced by $\omega t^{\ge0}H\to\omega H$. The projection to $H^0(\operatorname{gr}^0H)=\bigoplus_p\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{gr}^pM,\operatorname{gr}^pN)$ sends a morphism to its graded morphisms.
On the full finite-coefficient bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories, the exact étale/pro-étale comparison of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] induces an equivalence of these finite filtered categories with the classical filtered étale categories, namely the categories obtained by the construction of [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category] from the abelian category of sheaves of $A$-modules on the small étale site of $X$ (bounded complexes, finite filtrations, localization at graded quasi-isomorphisms, every graded piece bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude), compatible with $\omega$, every $\operatorname{gr}^p$, the filtered operations, and their displayed adjunction and trace-construction transformations.

source.place: §5.1.2(b,c), Lemma 5.1.4, §5.1.5, §5.2.1(b)–5.2.2; filtered operations and Hom comparison; the finite-coefficient étale/pro-étale comparison is the filtered extension of lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin (finite filtrations)

proof.text: Work first in finite filtered complexes of an abelian category. In an enclosing universe the dg category of such complexes has Hom complex consisting of filtration-preserving graded maps, with differential $d(h)=d_Nh-(-1)^{|h|}hd_M$. It satisfies (A),(B),(C) of [lem-coef-dg-abc-homotopy-category-triangulated]: direct sums and shifts carry the termwise filtrations; the cone of $u$ has terms $N^i\oplus M^{i+1}$, filtration $F^pN^i\oplus F^pM^{i+1}$, and differential $(d_N,u;0,-d_M)$. The admissible sequence $N\to C(u)\to M[1]$ has the displayed degreewise inclusions/projections and boundary $u[1]$. Hence the filtered homotopy category is triangulated, also with bounded cochain degrees. The objects whose every grade is acyclic form a full replete triangulated subcategory: graded cones and shifts are ordinary cones and shifts, so [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] applied to a graded cone gives closure under triangles. Apply [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] and [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6]. The cone class is exactly the graded quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the localization of [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category] is triangulated with cone triangles. Passing from chain maps to filtered homotopy classes makes no difference to the localization: the filtered cylinder of $M$ is the direct sum of $M$ and its contractible identity cone; its projection to $M$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism, so homotopic maps become equal. All constructions preserve a common finite filtration interval. The same argument without a cochain bound gives $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$.

source.place: Filtered derived categories, construction by cones; Varshavsky §§5.1.1–5.1.2. General cone triangulation and localization supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text: The module-sheaf category is Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] for the bounded filtration-truncation functors and their natural distinguished triangles. Graded functors are exact since they commute with shifts and cones. For the unbounded finite-filtered $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$, the same representative calculation works: truncations retain a grade or replace it by zero, and the cone projection $C(F^pM\to M)\to M/F^pM$ is the identity below $p$ and the projection of a contractible identity cone to zero at or above $p$. Thus it is a graded quasi-isomorphism and identifies the cone triangle with the truncation triangle. Forgetting filtration preserves graded quasi-isomorphisms: apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] successively to $0\to F^{i+1}M\to F^iM\to\operatorname{gr}^iM\to0$, over the finite filtration interval. Forgetting also commutes with cones and shifts, so is exact. In both bounded and unbounded categories, if every grade of $M$ is zero then $0\to M$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism and becomes invertible. Applying this to a cone also proves detection of isomorphisms.

Apply [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$, which has enough injectives by step 2. Its bounded finite-filtered localization is exactly the category of [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category]. It supplies the filtered global Hom $H\in DF^+(\mathbf{Ab})$, the identification $\omega H\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_X(\omega M,\omega N)$, and $\operatorname{gr}^rH\simeq\bigoplus_p R\operatorname{Hom}_X(\operatorname{gr}^pM,\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}N)$. View $H$ in $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$ through the fully faithful bounded-below inclusion of [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison]. This inclusion is induced by the same complexes and graded quasi-isomorphisms, so it preserves forgetting, grades and filtration truncations. The formula is the requested one with $q=p+r$.

The morphism-computation clause of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^bF}(M,N)\simeq H^0(\omega t^{\ge0}H)$. Its next two clauses identify the actual maps: forgetting is induced by $\omega t^{\ge0}H\to\omega H$, and projection to $H^0(\operatorname{gr}^0H)$ has components $\operatorname{gr}^pu$. Under the fully faithful embeddings of [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison], this is the bounded filtered Hom group of the statement and the same inclusion/projection for the object $H$ in $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$. Thus no further global-Hom construction or comparison is needed.

Choose $N\to I$ from [lem-trf-filtered-localization-injective-model] and define the sheaf Hom complex with $F^r\mathcal Hom^\bullet(M,I)$ consisting of maps sending $F^pM$ into $F^{p+r}I$. On every slice site, restriction of an injective module sheaf is injective: by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] it has the left adjoint extension by zero, which is exact (also [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-preserves-exact]), so Hom into the restriction is Hom into an injective composed with an exact functor. Split each finite filtered injective target term by splitting its top injective subobject and repeating on the quotient. A map to its grade-$q$ summand $J_q$ in filtration degree $r$ is a map $M/F^{q-r+1}M\to J_q$. Restriction to $F^{q-r}M/F^{q-r+1}M$ is surjective by injectivity; its kernel is the condition for degree $r+1$. Consequently restriction gives the canonical, splitting-independent graded sheaf-complex isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}^r\mathcal Hom^\bullet(M,I)\simeq\bigoplus_p\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{gr}^pM,\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}I)$. The ordinary internal-Hom model [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] applies to these bounded-below injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. It proves descent on grades under changes of source or injective resolution, hence descent in the finite filtered localization. This defines $R\mathcal Hom^F$ with the stated grades and underlying internal Hom. Chain Hom takes cones to the signed Hom cones in both variables, proving exactness after resolution. The package [prop-functor-package] supplies bounded ctf outputs for each grade; the finite number of grades and the bounded-representative clause of [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] give a bounded filtered ctf output.

Take split-flat resolving models $P\to M$ and $Q\to N$ from [lem-trf-finite-filtered-flat-resolution]. Form their ordinary total tensor with $F^r=\sum_{p+q=r}\operatorname{im}(F^pP\otimes F^qQ)$. In every pair of cochain degrees the chosen splittings identify this filtration with the sum of the components whose grade sum is at least $r$. Projection modulo $F^{r+1}$ consequently gives a canonical, splitting-independent map from $\bigoplus_{p+q=r}\operatorname{gr}^pP\otimes\operatorname{gr}^qQ$ to grade $r$, and the split calculation proves it is an isomorphism. It commutes with the tensor differential, including its Koszul sign, so holds after totalization. The resolution node gives K-flatness of each grade and of the underlying complex, acyclicity preservation, and equivalence of the resolving localization. Thus total tensor descends in both variables, its forgetting is ordinary derived tensor, and its grade is the finite derived-tensor sum in the statement. Cones commute with total tensor, proving exactness in both variables. Apply the ctf tensor stability in [prop-functor-package] and the finite-grade bounded-representative assertion of [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] to restrict to the stated bounded domains.

Use [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the exact-tensor definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The ordinary chain tensor--Hom adjunction restricts to filtered maps: a map $P\otimes Q\to I$ preserves filtration exactly when its adjoint sends $F^pP$ into $F^p\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,I)$. It respects differentials and filtered homotopies. Choose $P,Q$ split-flat and bounded above by [lem-trf-finite-filtered-flat-resolution], and $I$ split-injective and bounded below by [lem-trf-filtered-localization-injective-model]. Terms of the shifting sheaf Hom from $Q$ to $I$ are finite sums of internal Homs from flat to injective modules. Such an internal Hom is injective, since its Hom functor is Hom into an injective composed with exact flat tensor. The cochain-index products are finite by the two opposite bounds. Thus this Hom is bounded below and filtered injective. To compute maps from a possibly unbounded-below resolving source, choose $c$ below its graded cohomological lower bound and below the target's first nonzero degree minus two. The good truncation of [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] gives a bounded source and changes no Hom terms in degrees $-1,0,1$. Its $H^0$ is therefore unchanged, and the bounded-source injective comparison applies. This applies also to the tensor source. Descending the chain bijection proves the filtered tensor--Hom adjunction. Evaluation, units and associativity/composition use these chain formulas, so forget to the ordinary maps. Apply [lem-trf-filtered-bifunctor-graded-comparison] to the lifts just constructed: their support intervals add for tensor and subtract for internal Hom, by steps 5–6. Its transformation clause gives the canonical ordinary graded maps for supplied lifted transformations.

source.place: §5.2.2, filtered tensor--Hom adjunction; Lemma 5.1.4(i)–(iii) applied through the cited bifunctor comparison node.

proof.text: For $f^*$, $Rf_*$, $j_!$, and the supplied compactification composite $Rf_!$, apply [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts]. Its statement supplies the filtered adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ and the identity, composition, proper, compactification and unit--square--counit exchange maps, with exactly the asserted forgetful and graded maps. Apply [prop-functor-package] to their stated ctf domains; it supplies the ordinary bounded constructible landing, finite Tor conditions, compactification comparisons, and base-change isomorphisms. Because only finitely many grades occur, the common-bound argument in [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] gives bounded filtered outputs. Every comparison declared invertible by the package is invertible after filtering: its grade is that ordinary comparison by the lift theorem, and its cone has zero grades by step 2. This uses no exceptional adjunction outside the admissible package domain.

Place $\omega_X$ in filtration degree zero and put $D_X^FM=R\mathcal Hom^F(M,\omega_X)$. Step 5 and [lem-trf-filtered-bifunctor-graded-comparison] give $\operatorname{gr}^rD_X^FM=D_X\operatorname{gr}^{-r}M$ and a filtered biduality map defined by evaluation. Its grades are the usual biduality maps, isomorphisms by [thm-fix-general-biduality], so step 2 makes this a filtered anti-equivalence on the ctf category. Following §5.2.1(b), define the filtered exceptional pair by $Rf_!^F=D_Y^FRf_*^FD_X^F$ and $Rf^{!F}=D_X^Ff^{*F}D_Y^F$ on the domains of [prop-functor-package]. Their underlying functors are the named ordinary functors by its Verdier exchange and exceptional-dual formulas. Their adjunction follows from the three bijections
$\operatorname{Hom}(D_YRf_*D_XM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(D_YN,Rf_*D_XM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*D_YN,D_XM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,D_Xf^*D_YN)$.
All are now filtered bijections, using the ordinary filtered adjunction of step 8 and filtered biduality. Both contravariant reversals cancel, giving the same grade index for $Rf_!$ and $Rf^!$. This defines the exceptional unit and counit with their ordinary graded maps. We use these duality-defined filtered exceptional operations for the six-operation system, as in the source; step 8 separately constructed a compactification model. Step 10 constructs transformations for this duality-defined system. There is no use here of an exceptional adjunction for the compactification model before it has been constructed.

Apply the recursive construction of §5.2.2 to the duality-defined exceptional system of step 9. Its generators are the ordinary filtered adjunction of step 8, the exceptional adjunction of step 9, tensor--Hom adjunction and evaluation of step 7, pullback-composition identifications, and inverses of their specified comparison isomorphisms. For example an exchange mate is the composite inserting the unit, the commuting-square pullback identification and the counit. Composition of right adjoints is the mate of the pullback-composition identification; the corresponding exceptional composition is its dual. Projection/evaluation maps are the tensor--Hom adjoints of the associated evaluation composites. These prescriptions are precisely the canonical ordinary prescriptions, now applied to filtered adjunctions. The compactification, proper and exchange data supplied by [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] are the unary initial maps, and [prop-functor-package] supplies the ordinary domains and comparisons. Forgetting each recursively constructed map yields that ordinary map; [lem-trf-filtered-bifunctor-graded-comparison] and the unary lift theorem identify its grades with the ordinary prescriptions too. Whenever the ordinary prescription is an isomorphism, its filtered cone has zero grades, so the map has an inverse by step 2. Compositions, whiskering and inverses preserve all of these comparisons. Thus the adjunction, base-change, evaluation and trace-construction transformations asserted in the item have the required lifts; the argument uses their defining adjunction formulas, not an assertion about arbitrary natural transformations of triangulated functors.

Exactness of $\nu_X^*$ from [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] makes its termwise application preserve subquotients, cones and graded quasi-isomorphisms. It therefore defines a filtered comparison commuting with $\omega$, $t$ and all grades. Restrict to finite ctf graded pieces by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and both directions of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. For pure objects supported in grades $p,q$, filtered Hom into a pure injective resolution is ordinary derived Hom if $p\le q$, and zero if $p>q$; this follows directly from the filtration-preserving-map condition and [lem-trf-filtered-localization-injective-model]. The bounded-localization comparison [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] identifies these computations with bounded filtered Hom. The ordinary constructible derived equivalence thus gives bijections on these Hom groups, in every cochain shift. Apply the finite truncation triangles successively in the source and target, and [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] (also in the opposite triangulated category) to their exact Hom sequences. The diagram chase proves bijectivity for every pair: lift a desired map using the two neighboring bijections, correct its lift by the preceding boundary, and use the following bijection to test its obstruction; the same chase with a zero image proves injectivity. This proves full faithfulness of filtered comparison. For essential surjectivity induct on the finite number of grades: lift a pure graded piece by the ordinary equivalence and the remaining filtration by induction, lift their connecting morphism by full faithfulness, and take its cone shifted to realize the required extension triangle. Tor-amplitude reflection ensures the lifted grades are in the étale ctf domain. This is an equivalence of the actual bounded finite-filtered localizations specified in the statement, not a replacement category of arbitrary diagrams in the derived category.

source.place: §5.1.2, finite-filtration induction; comparison assembled from the cited finite-coefficient results

proof.text: Choose the filtered six-operation constructions on the étale side and transport them through the filtered equivalences of step 11. For the underlying unary operations, [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing] gives the ordinary comparisons for $f^*,Rf_*,j_!$ and the compactification definition of $Rf_!$. Its hypotheses hold: $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, and all the schemes and morphisms are in the standing finite-type setting. The finite ctf inputs lie in the stated localizing closures. The Verdier exchange and biduality clauses of [prop-functor-package] identify the compactification $Rf_!$ with the duality-defined operation used in step 9. Thus these transported functors forget to the specified pro-étale functors.

For tensor, use split-flat representatives from [lem-trf-finite-filtered-flat-resolution]. The exact module inverse image of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] preserves images, quotients and finite sums. Hence it carries the convolution step $\sum_{p+q=r}\operatorname{im}(F^pP\otimes F^qQ)$ to the corresponding convolution step of the pulled-back tensor complex. Module inverse image commutes with tensor and with the totalization sums, as in the K-flat tensor-pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. That node also states that the pulled-back flat K-flat models are flat K-flat. These give the filtered tensor comparison. On every grade it is exactly the sum of the ordinary tensor comparisons, by the representative calculation in step 6; these are isomorphisms by the same tensor-pullback node. Step 2 therefore makes the filtered comparison invertible.

For internal Hom, apply [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible] to the ordinary ctf inputs: its first input is ctf and its second is bounded constructible, as required. The evaluation-defined normalization of this comparison is explicit in [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. Consequently the ordinary internal Hom of the transported system is identified with the specified pro-étale one; both outputs belong to ctf by [prop-functor-package]. This replaces the inline Yoneda test of the returned proof by the existing comparison theorem, without introducing any site-perfectness assumption.

For $Rf^!$, use [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with the ordinary finite-ctf equivalences of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], restricted using [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], and the $Rf_!$ comparison of step 12. The two horizontal functors are equivalences, and the compared left adjoints are the compact-support functors, so the mate identifies their right adjoints wherever [prop-functor-package] admits them. For the structure morphism and the constant $A$, [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] explicitly identifies the dualizing objects and the evaluation-defined Verdier dualities. These are exactly the objects and dualities used to define the filtered exceptional operations in step 9. No adjoint outside the package's admitted domain is invoked.

Use [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] for the comparisons of adjunctions just obtained: its unit and counit equations identify the corresponding ordinary units and counits. Evaluation is the tensor--Hom counit, so satisfies the same equation. For the bifunctor transformations, [lem-trf-filtered-bifunctor-graded-comparison] identifies their graded maps with the ordinary graded transformations; the required filtered lifts and support bounds were constructed in steps 5–10. Every transformation of step 10 is a composite, whiskering or inverse of these generators. Applying the comparison to each generator gives the comparison for the composite; for an inverse use $c\,u^{-1}=v^{-1}c$ whenever $cu=vc$. This establishes the required transformation compatibility for the transported system.

For filtered global Hom apply [lem-trf-filtered-global-hom-exact-adjunction] with $L=\nu_X^*$ and $R=\nu_{X,*}$. These are the module-sheaf comparison adjoints, and $L$ is additive and exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. The two module-sheaf categories have enough injectives by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], applied on each small ringed site. The derived-unit hypothesis for every bounded-below object is precisely [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. The new node gives the filtered global-Hom isomorphism, its ordinary graded maps, and both Hom projection compatibilities. Its output lies in $DF^+(\mathbf{Ab})$; use [lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison] to view it in $DF(\mathbf{Ab})$, as in step 3. This completes the same finite-filtration comparison route as the returned step 12.
